chapter: War years, Goodman and Woody Herman
title: Traveling by car and train; a Toronto engagement
summary: They traveled by car and train to Rock Island, Winnipeg and Toronto, where drink had to be bought as set-ups.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: How did you travel, by car or by bus?
Two or three cars, or two cars?
As I remember. Sometimes we did. A couple of times we took the train out to Chicago.
In fact we took one train to Chicago, to Rock Island and a train up to Winnipeg and then the Canadian line over to Toronto.
And then we were there for Christmas. And Mildred came up for Christmas.
Where did you work in Toronto?
Out by the Kit -- wait a minute. It was out by the -- where the park was.
Yeah, Hyde Park or something up there.
Out that way, yeah. It was out in that district, there was a club there.
They didn't have liquor in Canada, then. You had to buy set-ups.
And a bottle. They had a local band there too, Benny Winestone was in it, I remember, and a few people.
